abilities.name: Divide and Conquer Search
abilities.description: Recursively partition problem space, eliminating halves based on comparison to find target in logarithmic time

parameters.partition_fn: Function to split problem into two halves
parameters.comparison_fn: Function to compare middle element with target
parameters.base_case_condition: When to stop recursion (usually when size <= 1)

examples: Finding square root via binary search
preconditions: Problem space can be ordered or partitioned
Comparison operation provides directional information
Problem exhibits monotonicity or similar property enabling elimination
postconditions: Time complexity reduced from O(n) to O(log n)
Space complexity O(1) for iterative or O(log n) for recursive
abilities.complexity_impact: Reduces time complexity from linear to logarithmic

abilities.name: Square Root Optimization
abilities.description: Use mathematical properties to reduce search space from O(n) to O(√n) by leveraging factor pairs or bounds

parameters.bound_function: Function that provides optimization bound (e.g., sqrt(n))
parameters.check_function: Function to test if a candidate satisfies conditions
parameters.iteration_direction: Direction to iterate (ascending, descending, or both)

examples: Prime number testing (check divisors up to √n)
preconditions: Problem has a mathematical property enabling bounds
Solution space exhibits symmetry or pairing
Upper bound can be computed efficiently
postconditions: Time complexity reduced from O(n) to O(√n)
abilities.complexity_impact: Reduces time complexity from linear to square root

abilities.name: Dynamic Programming with Memoization
abilities.description: Solve problems by breaking into overlapping subproblems and caching results to avoid recomputation

parameters.recurrence_relation: How to compute state from substates
parameters.cache_strategy: How to store and retrieve computed states

preconditions: Problem can be divided into subproblems
Subproblems overlap (same subproblems solved multiple times)
Optimal solution can be constructed from optimal sub-solutions
Subproblems have a finite, describable state space
postconditions: Time complexity often reduced from exponential to polynomial
Space complexity proportional to number of unique states
Solution builds up from base cases
abilities.complexity_impact: Reduces time complexity by eliminating redundant computation

abilities.name: Rate-Based Transformation
abilities.description: Convert between domains using an intermediate reference point or rate

parameters.rate_table: Mapping from domain A to reference and reference to domain B
parameters.reference_point: Common reference for conversion (e.g., USD for currency)
parameters.inverse_available: Whether inverse transformation is also available

examples: Currency conversion via USD as base
Unit conversion (metric to imperial via SI units)
preconditions: Conversion is transitive (A→B = A→RATE→B)
Reference point is stable or rates can be obtained
Transformation function is well-defined and invertible (or pseudo-invertible)
postconditions: Conversion possible even without direct A→B rate
Allows offline operation with cached rates
abilities.complexity_impact: Enables conversion with O(1) lookup after rate acquisition

abilities.name: Fault Tolerant Querying
abilities.description: Design queries that degrade gracefully with structured fallback responses

parameters.fallback_strategy: What to do when primary fails (alternative, partial, default)
parameters.error_handling: How to classify and respond to different error types
parameters.response_structure: Consistent format for success and failure responses

examples: DNS lookup returning structured response with availability status
API calls with circuit breaker pattern
Network requests with timeout and retry logic
preconditions: Query can fail in identifiable ways
Some value can be provided even when primary goal fails
Callers can handle structured responses
postconditions: System remains usable even when external services fail
User experience degrades gracefully rather than catastrophically
abilities.complexity_impact: Adds constant overhead for error handling but improves reliability

abilities.name: Iterative Refinement Loop
abilities.description: Progressively improve solution through feedback cycles and measurement

parameters.baseline_establishment: How to establish initial solution or state
parameters.feedback_mechanism: How to measure quality or identify issues
parameters.improvement_strategy: How to modify solution based on feedback
parameters.termination_condition: When to stop iterating (good enough, max iterations, convergence)

examples: Interactive currency converter with input validation
Auto-shutdown with configurable delay and confirmation
Debugging through hypothesis testing and fixing
preconditions: Baseline solution can be established
Feedback can be gathered about solution quality
Improvements can be made based on feedback
Process can converge or reach acceptable state
postconditions: Process terminates when goals met or no further improvement possible
Final solution better than initial baseline
abilities.complexity_impact: Adds iterative overhead but can dramatically improve solution quality
